calls.title: Nhat / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed the design of the filter user interface, emphasizing clarity and consistency while deciding to keep filters separate due to time constraints and user experience concerns. Kari Kay highlighted a stationary text filter with clear functions and the implementation of a dropdown for metric selection aimed at reducing visual clutter. The team coordinated on timelines, planning for a project handoff to Johnny, ensuring progress despite time zone challenges. They acknowledged the need for user-friendly designs that avoid overwhelming users with complex filter combinations, aiming for a clean and recognizable interface. Additionally, discussions touched upon the importance of consistent design standards across teams and the need for clearer documentation on filter components.
calls.keywords: filters, UI design, dropdown, metric selection, multi-select, experiment filters

calls.title: Nhat / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed refining the experiment and product analytics dashboard, emphasizing the need for a global filter integration set for the version 5.0 release, which will ensure date range filters apply uniformly across all sections. Redesigning filter labels and user interface elements was highlighted to enhance clarity, as current elements risk causing confusion. Simplifying dashboard filter overrides can improve user experience by consolidating controls. The comparison feature's UI was also noted for improvement, recommending a clearer method for displaying comparison periods. Overall, the team aims to balance speed of feature rollout with quality of UI enhancements to ensure usability.
calls.keywords: Global Filters, Experiment Dashboard, Filter UI, Date Range Compare, Dashboard Overrides, UX Redesign
